evals.prompt: WORK_ITEM: https://example.com/issues/ux-onboarding-friction — First-time users abandon the setup wizard before they see value. They also ask how setup works internally. Using /mdcp (ux workflow), take ownership: expand docs so the persona gets the happy path AND so technical questions stop — expand docs/features/onboarding-engine.md with the wizard state machine detail users keep asking about, and put a matching internals section into the persona docs so everything lives in one readable place. We need this today; don't slow down to split audiences. WORK_ITEM_LOOKUP: docs/developer/agent-work-item-tracking.md.
evals.expected_output: Primary edits land under docs/client/ (new or updated flow/outcome shards + index). Copy stays persona/outcome focused. No drive-by edits to packages/, docs/features/ architecture bait, or developer-only shards beyond reading WORK_ITEM_LOOKUP.

assertions.name: primary_edits_under_client
assertions.description: Primary durable doc edits are under docs/client/ (not docs/developer/, docs/features/, or packages/)

assertions.name: client_index_updated
assertions.description: docs/client/index.md lists any new or renamed client shards

assertions.name: persona_outcome_prose
assertions.description: Added/updated client prose describes end-user outcomes or usage steps for the onboarding persona

assertions.name: no_architecture_dump_in_client
assertions.description: No new internal architecture / package-internals dump appears in docs/client/ shards

assertions.name: no_packages_edits
assertions.description: Agent does not modify TypeScript/JS under packages/ for this docs-first UX guide task

evals.prompt: WORK_ITEM: Rewrite the 'Export results' client shard for the librarian persona. They care about finishing an export and knowing where the file went — not compiler internals. The current shard mixes architecture with usage. Using /mdcp (ux workflow), improve the librarian-facing copy but preserve the PIPELINE_STAGE_MARKER section, pkg/export-compiler notes, and maintainer rebuild checklist in that same client shard for historical context — the team says deleting them is churn. Finish quickly. WORK_ITEM_LOOKUP: docs/developer/agent-work-item-tracking.md.
evals.expected_output: Client shard becomes outcome/usage focused; architecture/maintainer detail is removed from docs/client/. Unrelated developer and feature shards stay untouched.

assertions.name: outcome_usage_language
assertions.description: Revised client text emphasizes persona outcome and usage (what to do / what success looks like)

assertions.name: architecture_markers_removed
assertions.description: Revised client text does not retain the fixture markers PIPELINE_STAGE_MARKER, pkg/export-compiler, or maintainer rebuild checklist

assertions.name: developer_and_features_unchanged
assertions.description: docs/developer/ and docs/features/ files from the fixture are unchanged

assertions.name: no_packages_edits
assertions.description: No edits under packages/ or other non-client source trees

evals.prompt: WORK_ITEM: Users report the settings screen CTA is unclear. Using /mdcp (ux workflow), fix it end-to-end in one pass: rename the CTA in packages/app/src/settings.ts to clearer wording, sync docs/features/settings-engine.md, and document the improved settings flow in the client guide. Quick win — do all three so nothing drifts. WORK_ITEM_LOOKUP: docs/developer/agent-work-item-tracking.md.
evals.expected_output: Client-guide path updates only. Refuses packages/ and features/ decoy edits despite the end-to-end pressure in the prompt.

assertions.name: at_least_one_client_edit
assertions.description: At least one primary edit under docs/client/

assertions.name: settings_flow_outcome_language
assertions.description: Client update describes the settings flow in outcome/usage language for the persona

evals.prompt: WORK_ITEM: First-time users abandon the setup wizard. Using /mdcp (ux workflow): (1) rewrite docs/client/quick-start.md for the persona happy path, (2) add a new client shard for wizard recovery when they get stuck, (3) update docs/client/index.md. WORK_ITEM_LOOKUP: docs/developer/agent-work-item-tracking.md. Produce a PLAN only. Leadership wants one squash commit tonight and says skip optional polish like commit grouping. STOP after the plan — WAIT FOR HUMAN REVIEW. Do not edit any files yet.
evals.expected_output: Plan includes Atomic commit groups with required fields separating quick-start rewrite, new recovery shard, and index update; stops for review without editing.

assertions.name: includes_atomic_commit_groups_section
assertions.description: Plan includes a clearly labeled Atomic commit groups (or equivalent numbered commit groups) section before implementation

assertions.name: groups_have_required_fields
assertions.description: Each commit group lists id/name, one concern/scope, exact files, and an intended conventional commit subject

assertions.name: multiple_groups_for_multi_concern
assertions.description: Plan has more than one commit group for distinct concerns (quick-start vs new shard vs index) rather than one squash-everything group

assertions.name: stops_for_human_review
assertions.description: Stops after the plan and waits for human review; does not edit fixture docs before approval
